text:
maria: Quick q — how should the API gateway evaluate model selection when we have both an x-model-alias header and per-route pining?
jon: Are you asking precedence between route config pin vs header-provided alias? :thinking:
maria: Yeah. Example: route has pin to `redwood-chat@v2.3` for latency guarantees, but caller sends `x-model-alias: redwood-chat:latest`. Which wins?
sophie: Current impl does header alias > route default alias, but route "pin" was supposed to be a hard override for safety. I think that mismatch is a bug.
tim: We purposely made alias mutable from caller for flexibility, but pins should be able to force a version when set as `pin_mode: strict`. There's also `pin_mode: advisory` for telemetry-only.
adarsh: Proposed rule: 1) If route sets `pin_mode: strict` -> honor pinned version and ignore header alias. 2) If route sets `pin_mode: advisory` -> use header alias but add telemetry flag and a rollout-check. 3) If no pin -> use header alias or default alias.
maria: That maps to what I expected. Need to account for compatibility constraints though — e.g., pinned model might not support kv-cache or longer context.
jon: Right. We should validate compatibility before honoring a pin. If pinned model lacks required capability, fallback to next compatible variant and emit alert.
sophie: Suggest adding config snippet for clarity:

```
route: /v1/chat
match: path_prefix
model_alias: redwood-chat
pin: redwood-chat@v2.3
pin_mode: strict # strict | advisory | none
compatibility_requirements:
  kv_cache: true
  max_seq: 2048
fallback_order:
  - redwood-chat@v2.2
  - redwood-chat@v2-quant
```

maria: Nice. Also want header-level overrides for debugging via an admin token, but only allowed when `pin_mode != strict` unless an emergency override flag is present.
tim: Emergency override path should be gated by RBAC and logged to an "override" telemetry stream so we can audit.
adarsh: Telemetry note: emit fields `route_pin_applied`, `header_alias`, `model_selected`, `compatibility_mismatch` and `fallback_used` so console dashboards can show rollouts/quality correlation.
jon: For quotas & cost accounting, we also need to tag tokens with the actual model variant used, not the alias. Otherwise billing is wrong.
sophie: Rollouts UX: Console should allow admins to set pin TTLs (e.g., 24h) and rollout windows. If a pin expires, route falls back to alias/default and we send a slack/ops alert.
maria: How should we store pins? Per-route config + an optional per-customer override table?
adarsh: Store canonical pins in control plane config (replicated). Customer overrides live in their tenant metadata with a higher precedence but still subject to `pin_mode` rules.
tim: Don't forget cache invalidation: KV cache schemas depend on model version. When we switch selected model, we must flush per-tenant KV cache or mark entries with model-version tags. Otherwise you'll get decode errors.
jon: Good call. Implementation checklist: validate compatibility at decision time, tag/flush caches on model switch, log model variant for billing & tracing, enforce RBAC for emergency overrides, expose telemetry fields, TTL for pins.
maria: Can we add a tiny e2e test that simulates a pinned route with header alias and incompatible capability to ensure fallback and alerting trigger?
adarsh: I'll add an integration test to eng-platform CI. Pseudocode:

```
# test: pinned route incompatible kv_cache
deploy route with pin redwood-chat@v2.3 (kv_cache=false)
send request with x-model-alias: redwood-chat:latest and requires kv_cache=true
expect selected_model == redwood-chat@v2.2
expect telemetry.compatibility_mismatch == true
expect billing.tag == "redwood-chat@v2.2"
```

deploy-bot: config applied to staging at 2026-11-05T14:12:03Z :white_check_mark:
maria: thanks. Last question — ordering between header alias and tenant-level overrides?
sophie: Precedence: route pin(strict) > tenant override (if permitted by route) > header alias > route default alias. We'll document exact precedence in API gateway docs.
tim: I'll open a small RFC doc and a console mock for TTL UX. Want to avoid confusing product folks with too many knobs.
maria: cool. I'll file the follow-up RFC and link tests. :thumbsup:
